root_cause.text: In Bluetooth SSP event handlers `hci_user_passkey_notify_evt()` and `hci_keypress_notify_evt()`, the code looked up an `hci_conn` and accessed its fields without holding `hci_dev_lock`, allowing concurrent connection teardown to free the `hci_conn` and causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “hci_conn lookup and field access must be covered by hdev lock ... otherwise the connection can be freed concurrently,” and the patch fixes this by moving `hci_dev_lock(hdev)` before `hci_conn_hash_lookup_ba()` and keeping it held until all `conn` accesses and notifications are complete, with new `unlock:` paths replacing prior early `return`s.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “hci_conn lookup and field access must be covered by hdev lock ... otherwise the connection can be freed concurrently,” and the patch fixes this by moving `hci_dev_lock(hdev)` before `hci_conn_hash_lookup_ba()` and keeping it held until all `conn` accesses and notifications are complete, with new `unlock:` paths replacing prior early `return`s.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect passkey notification connection handling with the device lock and ensure the no-connection path exits via unlock.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_dev_lock(hdev) was added before looking up the ACL connection, and the early return on a failed hci_conn_hash_lookup_ba() was changed to jump to an unlock path instead of returning immediately.
intent_record.how: This makes the connection lookup and subsequent state update execute under the device lock, preventing unsynchronized access to hdev connection state, and avoids exiting through the no-connection path without releasing the lock by routing control flow to the unlock label.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a shared unlock target in `hci_user_passkey_notify_evt()` so all relevant execution paths can reliably release the device lock.
intent_record.what: A new label `unlock:` was added immediately before the existing `hci_dev_unlock(hdev);` call at the end of `hci_user_passkey_notify_evt()`.
intent_record.how: This enables control flow within the function to jump to a common unlock path, ensuring the device lock can be released from additional code paths without duplicating the unlock call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect keypress notification connection handling with the device lock and route early exits through unlock cleanup.
intent_record.what: The change adds a call to hci_dev_lock(hdev) at the start of hci_keypress_notify_evt(), changes the early return when no connection is found to jump to an unlock path, and replaces the return in the HCI_KEYPRESS_STARTED case with a jump to the same unlock path.
intent_record.how: This makes the handler execute while holding the device lock and ensures early-exit paths release that lock via a shared unlock label, preventing unlocked access to connection state and avoiding lock leaks or inconsistent state when processing keypress notification events.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix hci_keypress_notify_evt() to always unlock hdev by routing the completed keypress path through a common unlock exit.
intent_record.what: In hci_keypress_notify_evt(), the HCI_KEYPRESS_COMPLETED case was changed from returning immediately to jumping to a new unlock label, and a call to hci_dev_unlock(hdev) was added at that label at the end of the function.
intent_record.how: This ensures the device lock is released even when the keypress notification type is HCI_KEYPRESS_COMPLETED, preventing an early-exit path from leaving hdev locked and avoiding potential deadlocks or stuck behavior in later code.

grouping_result.intent: Fix hci_keypress_notify_evt() to always unlock hdev by routing the completed keypress path through a common unlock exit.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure HCI passkey and keypress notification event handlers correctly hold and always release the device lock by routing all exit paths through shared unlock cleanup.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: they add hci_dev_lock protection around hci_conn lookup/use in the passkey and keypress SSP event handlers and ensure all paths release the lock safely, preventing the concurrent teardown use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This obtains the hci_conn pointer in the event handler without the device lock held. The root cause is that the looked-up connection could be concurrently torn down and freed before later dereferences, making this unlocked lookup the start of the UAF window.
This dereferences the looked-up hci_conn without holding hci_dev_lock. If the connection was concurrently freed after lookup, this write becomes a use-after-free.
This accesses multiple fields from conn after the unlocked lookup. Those field reads can hit freed memory if teardown races with the handler.
As in the passkey handler, this performs an unlocked lookup of hci_conn in the keypress handler, allowing concurrent teardown to invalidate the returned pointer before use.
This writes through the hci_conn pointer without holding hci_dev_lock. If conn was freed by concurrent teardown, this is a direct use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unlocked lookup returns an hci_conn pointer that can be concurrently torn down and freed before subsequent accesses in the SSP event handlers, creating the use-after-free window described in the root cause.
This dereferences and writes through the looked-up hci_conn without holding hci_dev_lock, so if teardown races after the lookup, this becomes a use-after-free.
This call reads multiple fields from conn after the unlocked lookup, so it can access freed memory if the connection is concurrently destroyed.
This write in the keypress notification handler uses the hci_conn pointer without the required device lock, making it a use-after-free if the connection was freed after lookup.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 92a25256f142d55e25f9959441cea6ddeabae57e
Author: Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 6 18:39:26 2012 +0300

    Bluetooth: mgmt: Implement support for passkey notification
    
    This patch adds support for Secure Simple Pairing with devices that have
    KeyboardOnly as their IO capability. Such devices will cause a passkey
    notification on our side and optionally also keypress notifications.
    Without this patch some keyboards cannot be paired using the mgmt
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the full bodies of the two relevant event handlers, which is sufficient to assess the race/UAF condition. In both newly added functions, the code performs `conn = hci_conn_hash_lookup_ba(hdev, ACL_LINK, &ev->bdaddr);` and then directly accesses fields of `conn` (`conn->passkey_notify`, `conn->passkey_entered`, `conn->dst`, `conn->type`, `conn->dst_type`) without any visible `hci_dev_lock`/unlock protection. Specifically, `hci_user_passkey_notify_evt()` does the lookup, then writes `conn->passkey_notify = __le32_to_cpu(ev->passkey);` and `conn->passkey_entered = 0;`, then calls `mgmt_user_passkey_notify(hdev, &conn->dst, conn->type, conn->dst_type, ...)`. Likewise, `hci_keypress_notify_evt()` looks up `conn`, mutates `conn->passkey_entered` in the switch, and then calls `mgmt_user_passkey_notify(...)` using `conn` fields. This matches the stated root cause: lookup and dereference of `hci_conn` without holding `hci_dev_lock`, allowing concurrent teardown and use-after-free. No fix is present here because there is no locking around the lookup/access sequence.
